chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Music in school: reading music and singing harmony
summary: She learned to read music in school, sang harmony from the school song book, and worked out harmony alone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you formally study music outside of school?
Well, no, not really. The only lessons I had was when I picked up the valve trombone and started to play.
As a child.
No.
You took music in school,
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
though. I sang in school.
Did you learn to read music then?

Yeah, we learned how to read music and I was singing harmony. We formed a trio when I was going to junior high school, two boys and myself, and we used to book ourselves into the different classes. We had our own circuit going for us. But I had never considered ---
Do you remember what you sang?
Yeah, all the songs from the song book, the "Skaters Waltz," and "Finikuli-Finikula" and things like that. We were good.
Do you remember any other titles?
I can't remember any more. We used the old school song book and picked up anything that we could sing harmony to. And we were just having fun.
Did you sing the lead?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

No, I sang harmony. I discovered I could sing harmony when I was quite young. Talking about the first World War, I discovered I could sing harmony to "Until We Meet Again," and so far as singing is concerned, I wanted very much to be part of a singing group, you know, because I liked a lot of the things that I had heard by singing groups and I wanted to dance the hard way. I used to send to New York, I had a subscription to Dance Magazine and I think they used to print maybe some elementary dance lessons and I used to try to teach myself to some routines, you know.
You did that alone?

Alone, yeah, alone. And I'd be home-working and tried to figure out the dance notations and get myself a few steps going. One of my cousins, one of my aunt's sons, he was a very good dancer, Jess Jackson, he was a tap dancer. He was self-taught but he used to dance and I used to try to imitate some of his steps. I don't know what happened. I guess I couldn't get up off the floor. I didn't have the elevation that I
